_: Root specification for the engine-coverage denominator. See docs/ENGINE_COVERAGE.md.
Every entry names symbols in the pinned instrumented build
a place control enters KiCad from outside. Everything transitively reachable from
the `work` roots is the engine; everything else is out of scope BY CONSTRUCTION,
`regex` and `exact` are matched against the demangled-free mangled symbol name

why: kicad/kicad_cli.cpp. Process entry. Reaches PGM_KICAD startup, argparse, the
COMMAND_ENTRY table walk and COMMAND::Perform. NOTE the `main` node is shared
with thirdparty/lemon/lemon.c, which gcovr excludes from the report anyway.
CLI::<X>_COMMAND::doPerform(KIWAY&) -- the 30 kicad-cli subcommands plus the
CLI::COMMAND base. These have to be roots rather than fall out of `main`,
because the COMMAND objects are file-scope statics (kicad/kicad_cli.cpp:124-176)
whose only constructor call is in _GLOBAL__sub_I_, and main dispatches through
COMMAND::Perform -> virtual doPerform. `per_symbol` gives one closure per
subcommand so a gap can be attributed to the verb that would reach it.
kicad-cli dlopen()s _pcbnew/_eeschema/_cvpcb.kiface and calls into them through
the KIFACE vtable (common/kiway.cpp:759 HandleJob, kiway.cpp KiFACE() ->
OnKifaceStart, common/project.cpp:433 and eeschema/erc/erc.cpp:1816 ->
IfaceOrAddress). A static reference graph cannot cross a dlopen boundary or an
indirect vtable call, so these are explicit roots.
THE RULE FOR CHOOSING THEM, applied to the KIFACE vtable in include/kiway.h:155:
root every KIFACE virtual whose SIGNATURE is free of GUI types. That excludes
exactly CreateKiWindow(wxWindow*,int,KIWAY*,int) and HandleJobConfig(JOB*,
wxWindow*) -- the two that hand back or take a window -- and GetActions(
std::vector<TOOL_ACTION*>&), which is the interactive tool framework. It is a
mechanical rule over a 12-entry interface, not a curated file list, and
`assert_unreachable` below turns it into a checkable claim.
SaveFileAs, ProjectChanged, CancelPreload and PreloadLibraries are rooted even
though no kicad-cli path is known to call SaveFileAs: rooting them can only
widen the denominator, which is the safe direction for a coverage figure.
Static initialisers of every object in the build. These genuinely execute on
every kicad-cli invocation (or every kiface load), so their lines are trivially
'covered' -- that is the inflation behind cli/jobs' 43.9%. They are also load-
bearing: KiCad registers DRC test providers, IO plugins and settings schemas
from file-scope statics, so a closure that ignored them would MISS real engine
code. Kept, and kept SEPARATE: engine_report.py reports work-reachable lines
and init-only lines as two columns.

gui.excluded.CreateKiWindow.why: Returns a wxWindow*. The whole editor-frame/tool/dialog tree hangs off it.

gui.excluded.HandleJobConfig.why: Takes a wxWindow* parent; its only caller is kicad/dialogs/panel_jobset.cpp.

why: THE SIGNATURE RULE, applied to every function rather than just the KIFACE
vtable: a function that takes or returns a top-level wxWidgets GUI type, or a
wxWidgets *event*, cannot be called by kicad-cli -- it never constructs a window
and never runs an event loop. Matched on the Itanium-mangled name, so the
`<length><name>` form makes it an exact token match, not a substring guess.
`[0-9]wx[A-Za-z]*Event` is the whole wxEvent family (wxCommandEvent,
wxMouseEvent, wxPaintEvent, wxPanGestureEvent, ...).
`8wxWindow` IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT, and this is the clearest case of the
validation earning its keep. It was in this list until the positive probe
(docs/ENGINE_COVERAGE.md 6.1) showed `pcb drc --refill-zones` executing 95 lines
of pcbnew/zone_filler.cpp that the barrier had just moved out of scope: KiCad's
ZONE_FILLER_TOOL::FillAllZones( wxWindow* aCaller, ... ) takes a wxWindow* that
the CLI simply passes as nullptr. A wxWindow* parameter is very often an
OPTIONAL PARENT, not a proof of GUI-ness. wxDialog/wxFrame/wxTopLevelWindow and
the event family do not have that escape hatch.
KiCad's own TOOL_EVENT is likewise not matched, for the same reason.
Needed because RTA seeds off constructors: a file-scope static of a class whose
vtable contains window-taking methods re-imports the GUI through the back door.
Measured effect (2026-08-05): the `gui` bucket's contribution to the engine
denominator, and `common/bitmap_info.cpp`'s 5090-line icon table, which reached
the closure only through BITMAP_STORE's wxBitmap accessors.
VALIDATED: adding this barrier must not increase the executed-but-out-of-scope
count (`engine_validate.py negative`). If it does, it has cut something the
suite demonstrably runs, and it is wrong.
TOOL_INTERACTIVE::setTransitions() is where each interactive tool binds its
TOOL_EVENT handlers. A CLI run has no TOOL_DISPATCHER and no event loop, so no
transition is ever taken -- but every tool's constructor calls it, which made it
the single RTA hub that pulled the whole editor tool set into scope (it is the
edge that put EDA_3D_CANVAS::DisplayStatus 13 hops from a CLI root).
This does NOT exclude tool code the CLI genuinely uses: ZONE_FILLER_TOOL is
called directly by the DRC/refill path, and the probe run in
`docs/ENGINE_COVERAGE.md` 6.1 executes 33 of its lines with this barrier in
place.

_deferred_cut_note: These are BARRIERS, not roots. The closure is computed twice -- once normally,
once with these nodes never entered -- and the difference is the code that only
a deferred CLI path can reach. A per-verb closure cannot answer this, because
IFACE::HandleJob dispatches on job type and so reaches every job handler from
the single kiface root; cutting the entry point is the only separable question.
Both halves of each verb have to be cut: the kicad-cli-side doPerform AND the
kiface-side handler, because the two are in different binaries and the handler
is reachable from the jobs-handler constructor, not from doPerform.
